   CITY OF BEVERLY HILLS

  POLICY AND MANAGEMENT

  MEMORANDUM

 TO:  City Council Liaison / Chamber of Commerce Committee
 FROM:  Magdalena Davis, Community Outreach Manager

 DATE:  June 2, 2026

 SUBJECT:  Update on Fiscal Year 2025-2026 Quarters Three and Four Programs and
  Initiatives for the Beverly Hills Chamber of Commerce

 ATTACHMENT:  1. Beverly Hills Chamber of Commerce Q3 and Year-to-Date
  Presentation
  2. Work Plan Trackers (General Workplan and Marketing Specific)

INTRODUCTION
This item provides the City Council Chamber of Commerce Committee Liaisons Mayor Corman
and Vice Mayor Wells (Liaisons) an update of the programs and initiatives of the Beverly Hills
Chamber of Commerce (Chamber) during quarters three and quarter four (up to last week) of
Fiscal Year 2025-2026. As a reminder, it includes Liaison review and approval of reallocations of
meetings.

DISCUSSION
The Beverly Hills Chamber of Commerce is contracted by the City to provide a range of economic
development programs which reflect City priorities, seek to retain existing businesses, and attract
new businesses to Beverly Hills. The Chamber’s focus is on economic development for the
community, fostering business-to-business relationships, and to act as a liaison between the City
and business community. An agreement detailing the workplan between the City and Chamber
was approved for FY 25/26 on July 1, 2025, and states that the Chamber will provide quarterly
updates on programs and initiatives.

The workplan for FY 25/26 also included the carryover workplan items for FY 24/25 which included
one Small Business Task Force Meeting and one Property Owners Task Force Meeting. These
carryovers would have been carried out in FY 25/26, in addition to the four required meetings for
the current Fiscal Year, but the Chamber received approval that they be allocated towards
different public meetings to best serve the business community.

The Chamber will provide a more detailed update of their workplan items during the presentation of
the meeting (Attachment 1). Updates will include all activity for quarter 3 (Q3) and up to date
information for quarter four (Q4):
   New York Business Attraction and Retention Mission updates on results to date
   Miami Business Attraction and Retention Mission updates on results to date
   Marketing and outreach support for City and Partner events, functions, and initiatives,
  including former Mayor initiatives, partner marketing, and online business guides
     Property Owner’s Task Force (3 of 5 – 1 Carryover from FY 24/25, and 2 meetings from
  this current year to be reallocated)
    Small Business Task Force (3 of 5 – 1 Carryover from FY 24/25, and 2 meetings from this
  current year to be reallocated)
    Mayoral Business Retention Meetings (9 of 12) – 3 scheduled to occur
    New Businesses Newsletter (3 of 4)
    Broker’s Roundtable (1 of 2 retail, and 2 of 2 office)
    Metro Subway Stakeholder Meetings (9 of 12 – 2 meetings reallocated to stakeholder
  meetings on Wilshire/La Cienega station opening, final meeting to be conducted)
    Walk the Neighborhood campaigns (19 of 24)
    Two previous Mayoral initiative events Spotlight with Sharona were completed during
  quarter three:
  o Rodeo Drive
  o N. Canon Drive
    Partner Marketing for Q3 and Q4 included city events such as Spotlight with Sharona,
  Evening of Unity, Miami Mission Trip campaigns also highlighted new businesses and
  ribbon cuttings, as well as community updates for BH Art Show, Metro opening, World
  Cup business outreach, Fire trespassing forms, etc.
    Social Media Campaigns and Newsletter for NOW Beverly Hills shop local program with
  vendor PSM had the best engagement of any quarter, with over 52,000 accounts reached
  on Meta (Instagram and Facebook). A full recap is in Attachment 1.
  o Quarter 3 included the launch of the Hidden in the Hills series, showcasing S.
  Robertson, and the best performing posts were the Alfreds Coffee window opening
  (reel) and Dine LA restaurants in Beverly Hills (static post)
  o Quarter 4 continued Hidden in the Hills on La Cienega, which benefitted from
  being a boosted post, and launched the Elevate Your Game series, in advance of
  the World Cup

Additionally, the NOW Beverly Hills has been and will continue collaborating with the City and
partners to cross-promote a full summer of soccer activities. The Chamber hosted 10 ribbon
cuttings for businesses during Q3 and Q4 so far with the special event permit fees waived, per
the approved workplan. A full tracker for the items can be found in Attachment 2.

Based on the completed tasks, the Chamber is on target for their workplan at the close of the
final quarter, and has committed to complete all the outstanding items before June 30. Scheduling
challenges for task force work, along with delayed work related to Metro functions have created
challenges to meeting workplan goals.

In order to more evenly distribute work throughout the year, and to avoid clustering task force
meetings in the latter quarters of the fiscal year, the Chamber reallocated 4 task force meetings,
which the City Manager and Liaisons approved, completed in Q3 and Q4:
   Education for the City’s Green Building Initiative in partnership with Public Works in
  March
   Metro Outreach meetings for Wilshire/La Cienega Station Opening in April in lieu of
  monthly Metro meetings from November and December
   Updating 2 guides for the business community: How to Do Business in Beverly Hills, and
  the regional Business Attraction Guide, which are in progress
 The Chamber has also adjusted the final Metro Outreach meeting for the year to be an in-person
tour of the station, rather than an online meeting, for June.

FISCAL IMPACT
There is no fiscal impact from reviewing this item as the funding was already accounted for in the
FY 25/26 Chamber contract in the total not to exceed amount of $553,245. Funding for the
Chamber’s total contract of $553,245 is funded through the Policy & Management Department’s
Business Development budget in the amount of $380,000, with the remaining $173,245 funded
from the Tourism and Marketing budget for Chamber initiatives which are tourism and marketing
focused. Metro related workplan expenses related to the Metro Purple Line Extension and are
reimbursable by Metro, and staff will continue to work with the Chamber to ensure reimbursement
for these expenses.

The Liaisons may want to consider a similar partner model should any workplan items not be
completed that instead of carrying forward the items, the funding is returned to the City. As of now,
the items are scheduled to reallocated instead.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends the Liaison Committee review and provide recommendations for the Chamber
of Commerce quarters three and four, to date, program and initiative updates for FY 25/26.

   CITY OF BEVERLY HILLS

  POLICY AND MANAGEMENT

  MEMORANDUM

 TO:  City Council Liaison / Chamber of Commerce Committee
 FROM:  Magdalena Davis, Community Outreach Manager

 DATE:  June 2, 2026

 SUBJECT:  Review of Fiscal Year 2026-2027 Workplan Funding Requests for the
  Beverly Hills Chamber of Commerce

 ATTACHMENT:  1. Beverly Hills Chamber of Commerce FY26-27 Proposed Work Plan
  2. FY26-27 Budget Details Sheet
  3. Liaison Presentation

INTRODUCTION
Each year the City enters into an agreement with the Beverly Hills Chamber of Commerce
(Chamber) to execute various work plan items, focused on economic sustainability, including
business development, marketing, and outreach for the upcoming fiscal year. This item provides
the City Council Chamber of Commerce Committee Liaisons Mayor Corman and Vice Mayor
Wells (Liaisons) an opportunity to review the Fiscal Year 2026/2027 (FY 26/27) work plan and
funding request from the Beverly Hills Chamber of Commerce and Civic Association (Chamber)
in the amount of $573,850.

Additionally, review is requested for FY 26/27 to waive special event permit fees, place of
assembly permit fees, and set flat rate reduced parking rates for specific Chamber signature
events, and ribbon cuttings hosted in partnership with the Chamber.

DISCUSSION
The City contracts with the Chamber to provide a range of economic development programs,
which reflect City priorities and seek to both retain existing businesses and attract new
businesses to Beverly Hills. The Chamber’s main focus is on fostering business-to-business
relationships in Beverly Hills and to act as a liaison between the City and business community.
Over the years, they have also expanded their scope of work to include marketing and outreach
that aligns with economic development, and have expanded the NOW Beverly Hills shop local
program, in partnership with the City.

The Chamber Liaisons are requested to review and make a recommendation on the Chamber
work plan and budget request for FY 26/27. It should be noted that the Chamber is traditionally
funded from two different City budgets – a set amount from the general fund, and the remainder
from TOT. For FY26/27, the increase would be absorbed entirely by the Tourism and Marketing
budget, for new and increasing activities related to promoting and marketing the City to attract
and retain businesses.
 The budget breakdown is as follows:
   $380,000 from the Business Development budget (General Fund)
   $193,850 from the Tourism & Marketing budget (Transient Occupancy Tax, or TOT)
   Total Request of $573,850

All of the City partners, including the Chamber, were of the flat TOT forecast for next fiscal year.

Review of Fiscal Year 2026-2027 Workplan and Funding Request
The Chamber’s proposed FY 26/27 work plan includes much of the programming and initiatives
that typically occur annually, as well as continuing the Miami Business Mission into a 3rd year.

The Chamber’s $40,120 can be accounted for in approximately $16,610 increased labor costs,
with the remaining funding of $26,210 in new initiatives. The line items with decreases include
marketing and outreach support, which has been reallocated towards the Now Beverly Hills shop
local program, another marketing effort, and the reduction in

The items proposed for elimination or adjustment include:
  - Reallocation in marketing – a decrease from City marketing and outreach support, to the
  Now Beverly Hills shop local program (another marketing effort)
  - Reduction in Task Force meetings – one each of the Small Business Assistance, and
  Property Owners groups, so that they are once approximately every 4 months (3 per fiscal
  year), rather than once a quarter (4 per fiscal year)
Beyond the increases to labor, the new or addition to initiatives that account for the increase
include:
  - An expansion of the Now Beverly Hills program, managed by vendor PSM, to include the
  creation and management of a TikTok social media account, and to retool the Now Beverly
  Hills newsletter to feature local community events, openings, cultural showings and other
  business events of interest, in order to increase exposure of the campaign, and gain more
  newsletter subscribers and social media followers, particularly focusing on attracting
  residents
  - National business attraction and retention – research, identification and outreach to
  business attraction targets nationwide that do not fall into the current New York or Miami
  trips; this will also include an update to the online guide for How to Do Business in Beverly
  Hills, and the Business Attraction guide. The metric goal is up to 30 businesses in one
  year.
  - Station activation for Wilshire and La Cienega subway are still in development, so the
  Chamber proposes to identify station activations that will promote economic opportunities
  at a late date, focusing their current workplan on a strategy for the future Beverly Drive
  station, instead. The metric goal for this is 3 stakeholder meetings and a written plan of
  action.
  o The Chamber does propose to continue evaluating potential station activations
  for the current La Cienega/Wilshire Metro station, in collaboration with Metro and
  the City, and would like to bring an item back, including a more defined scope of
  work and budget, should the Liaisons and Council feel this should be
  implemented.

  2 of 8
 Staff requests the Liaisons provide recommendations for the changes to the workplan above, and
review the following remaining work plan items. More detail is provided in Attachment 1, and a
breakdown of both the hard costs and labor costs, which account for the remainder of the increase
in costs, in Attachment 2.

  I.A. Chamber of Commerce will provide Marketing and Outreach Support for City and
  Partner Events, Functions, and Initiatives by providing marketing and communications
  support and business visitations to inform businesses about key resources and news
  updates and gather critical data and information for the City, Chamber and partners
  programs and initiatives. It includes but is not limited to Mayor and Council Priorities,
  Community Development or Sustainability initiatives, promotion of Concours event and
  Holiday programming, and more, such as the current World Cup promotions;

  I.B. Chamber of Commerce will organize and participate in the annual New York Business
  Attraction and Retention Mission setting up 24 meetings with companies in New York,
  including all research, preparation meetings and materials for the delegation, and follow-up
  required. The Chamber proposes to focus more on business attraction meetings to be
  conducted, with some business retention meetings, however the actual balance between
  retention and attraction meetings will be mutually agreed upon between the City and the
  Chamber prior to the trip’s finalization;

  I.C. Chamber of Commerce will manage regular meetings of the Beverly Hills Commercial
  Property Owner’s Task Force (3 meetings annually) to spur dialogue and develop ideas
  and plans for commercial properties;

  I.D. Chamber of Commerce will continue to manage the NOW Beverly Hills Shop Local
  Program, with vendor PSM as the creative agency. This program focuses on connecting
  businesses and residents, to encourage residents to shop locally. To achieve better
  marketing results across all businesses and neighborhoods, they propose to continue the
  social media accounts with a goal to increase engagement, produce 4 campaigns in total to
  occur quarterly, 12 newsletters to occur monthly, and ongoing cross-promotion with City
  programs, other City partners, and local businesses, as well as add the aforementioned
  enhancements to the newsletter and the brand new Now Beverly Hills TikTok account;

  I.E. Chamber of Commerce will organize and host Broker’s Roundtables so retail and office
  commercial real estate brokers can meet with each other, Chamber, and City staff to facilitate
  discussion on real estate opportunities that could benefit the community (4 total meetings
  per year: 2 focused on retail and 2 focused on office);

  I.F. Chamber of Commerce will provide management of Beverly Hills Small Business Task
  Force (3 meetings annually) to gather feedback and recommendations about strategies to
  attract and retain small businesses in Beverly Hills;

  3 of 8
 I.G. Chamber of Commerce will organize one-on-one Mayoral Business Retention
Meetings (12 in total) between Beverly Hills business owners and the Mayor to foster better
relationships and retention;

I.H. Chamber of Commerce will organize LA Metro Subway Stakeholder Outreach
Meetings. These meetings will provide a forum for businesses, partner agencies and the
City to communicate ongoing information about subway construction for Section 2 and its
impact to businesses (held monthly for a total of 12 meetings). Funds for this work plan item
are subject to reimbursement from Metro and are required to be tracked accordingly;

I.I. Chamber of Commerce will continue to implement action items from the City’s Economic
Sustainability Plan, however this item is proposed to continue to be updated annually only,
the same as the current fiscal year;

I.J. Chamber of Commerce will continue to push out the quarterly “New Business
Newsletter” (4 times a year) featuring “new” and “coming soon” businesses to help support
business attraction efforts of both the City and the Chamber of Commerce;

I.K. Chamber of Commerce proposes to continue the Miami Business Attraction Mission
which would now be in its 3rd year, including conducting the research necessary focused on
business attraction. This work plan item was successful this past fiscal year, and included
making it more closely match the New York trip with a goal of 24 meetings, as well as the
necessary marketing materials, business meeting research, and follow up. This year’s
proposed trip would match that 3-day, 24 meeting format, including all research, preparation
meetings and materials for the delegation, and follow-up required. Liaisons are requested to
give direction if the business attraction meetings to be conducted, and it is recommended
that the actual balance between retention and attraction meetings will be mutually agreed
upon between the City and the Chamber delegation prior to the trip’s finalization;

New Initiatives are the second category of the workplan:

II.A. The Chamber proposes a new initiative, dubbed National Business Attraction and
Retention, to research, identification, and outreach to business targets nationally that do not
fall into the current trips. The goal will include attracting qualified businesses to expand to
Beverly Hills and to capture businesses from other areas of the country that reach out to
Beverly Hills. As a part of this item, the Chamber will also update the current Beverly Hills
Business Attraction Guide and Guide for Opening and Maintaining a Business in Beverly
Hills, which are a part of the current fiscal year, being subbed in as reallocations from 2 of
each task force meetings not held. Metrics for this new initiative, beyond the guides, are up
to 30 businesses.

II.B. The Chamber proposes to work with the City, partner agencies and business and
community stakeholder to develop LA Metro Station Economic Development Strategy
and Station Activations for the future Beverly Drive Station in Beverly Hills. With the recent
opening comes an opportunity to identify an economic development strategy for the area

  4 of 8
   once construction has ceased including (1) what types of businesses the City and community
  would like to see in that area; (2) how to drive development in an appropriate and consistent
  manner; and (3) other potential ways to enhance the area once construction is completed.
  The Chamber proposes to manage a series of 3 stakeholder meetings of City staff, partner
  agencies (CVB, RDC), local businesses and other community stakeholders, and then
  develop a plan of action for implementation.

  III. A-E Chamber of Commerce is requesting a waiver of various permit fees and approval
  of parking flat rates for the following Chamber-hosted signature events, and ribbon cuttings
  in partnership with the City:
  A. Waive various permit fees for Chamber of Commerce signature event “Evening with
  the Mayor” (approximately $1,600)
  B. Waive various permit fees for Women’s Business Network “Women Who Shine Gala”
  (approximately $450)
  C. Waive various permit fees, personnel fees for Park Rangers and Public Works, and
  approve flat parking rates for Chamber of Commerce event “Innovate Beverly Hills”
  (approximately $3,700)
  D. Waive various permit fees, rental of Beverly Canon Gardens, personnel fees, and
  approve flat parking rates for Chamber of Commerce event “Summer Garden Party”
  (approximately $9,750)
  E. Waive various permit fees for Ribbon Cuttings (estimated totals x 12, approximately
  $15,800 total)

Please note the above requests are based on the current permit waivers, and the exact number
of businesses that would require permits for their ribbon cuttings are as-yet unknown. For the past
three fiscal years, City Council has approved the waiver of permit fees for specific Chamber of
Commerce Signature Events and Special Event Permit Fees for Chamber member ribbon
cuttings, along with providing discounted flat rate parking for supporting events. The full request
for these waivers are listed in Attachment 1 to this report.

The total estimated value of the fee waivers and flat parking rates are also detailed in Attachment
1 as provided by the Chamber, total approximately $31,300.

FISCAL IMPACT

For FY 26/27, the Chamber is requesting $573,850 as further detailed in Attachments 1 and 2.
Additionally, the Chamber is also requesting specific fee waivers, personnel waivers and flat
parking rates. The actual value for any fee waivers or flat parking rates will vary based on the actual
event, including the number of actual attendees and the extent of the event footprint.

The Chamber is traditionally funded from two different City budget sources; Business
Development Budget and from the Transient Occupancy Tax (TOT) Tourism and Marketing
Budget.

The FY 25/26 Business Development (00101313) budget, fixed at $380,000 for the past several
years post-pandemic, was included as part of next year’s budget by the Finance Department at the
June 5th budget meeting. Liaisons are requested to review funding in the amount of $380,000 of
the Chamber’s work plan from the Business Development budget. As several of the Chamber’s
initiatives are marketing focused, the remaining annual Chamber work plan funding has previously
come from the Tourism and Marketing budget, funded by Transient Occupancy Tax (TOT). The
current funding request requires $193,850 from the Tourism and Marketing budget, funded by
Transient Occupancy Tax (TOT).

The Finance Department is currently forecasting TOT revenue of $46,600,000 for FY 26/27, a flat
estimate from $46,000,000 for FY25/26. The Chamber was advised of this flat estimate. Staff
anticipates TOT funding would be allocated for various programs and partner agreements including
the request from the Chamber workplan. Other Council approvals include the RDC base funding
workplan, a portion of the Chamber of Commerce workplan, Holiday décor, the Holiday Lighting
Celebration on Rodeo Drive, the Concours d’Elegance Father’s Day Car Show, landscaping
funding, and trademark licensing intellectual property legal services.

Work plan expenses related to the Metro Purple Line Extension Section 2 ($16,025) are
reimbursable by Metro. Staff will work with the Chamber to ensure invoicing includes all Metro
required information to ensure reimbursement for these expenses.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends the Liaison Committee review and provide recommendations for the Beverly
Hills Chamber of Commerce Fiscal Year 2026-2027 Workplan and Funding Request, including:
  a. All items I-II as presented, including reallocations, reductions, and new initiatives;
  b. Items III permit waivers and flat-rate parking as presented;
  c. Recommendation of the funding allocations from the City’s Business Development
  budget and Tourism and Marketing Budget
